tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 1
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A nominal annual rate of $7.2\%$ compounded $4$ times per year has an effective annual rate of $7.40\%$ to the nearest $0.01$ percentage point.
An account starts at $\$7{,}000$ and grows continuously at $3.5\%$ for $4$ years. Its balance is $\$8{,}111.92$ to the nearest cent.
A single payment of $\$12{,}000$ is due in $4$ years. At an effective annual discount rate of $5.0\%$, its present value is $\$9{,}872.43$ to the nearest cent.
A grant pays $\$900$ in its first year and each annual payment is $4.0\%$ larger than the previous one. The total of the first $6$ payments is $\$6{,}034.68$ to the nearest cent.
An ordinary annuity pays $\$300$ at each month-end for $24$ months. At a monthly rate of $0.60\%$, its present value is $\$6{,}686.98$ to the nearest cent.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The effective annual rate compounds the periodic nominal rate over every period in the year.

$$R=\left(1+\frac{0.072}{4}\right)^{4}-1$$

$$R\approx 0.074000$$

$$100R\approx 7.40\%$$

The rounded effective rate is $7.40\%$, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

Continuous compounding applies the exponential accumulation factor.

$$FV=Pe^{rt}$$

$$FV=7000e^{0.035(4)}$$

$$FV\approx 8051.92$$

The continuous balance is $\$8{,}051.92$, not $\$8{,}111.92$, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

Present value divides the future payment by its full accumulation factor.

$$PV=\frac{12000}{(1+0.050)^{4}}$$

$$(1+0.050)^{4}\approx 1.215506$$

$$PV\approx 9872.43$$

The discounted value is $\$9{,}872.43$, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

A fixed percentage increase creates a finite geometric series.

$$S_{6}=a\frac{r^{6}-1}{r-1}$$

$$S_{6}=900\frac{1.04^{6}-1}{1.04-1}$$

$$S_{6}\approx 5969.68$$

The finite payment total is $\$5{,}969.68$, not $\$6{,}034.68$, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

An ordinary-annuity present value discounts a level payment made at each period-end.

$$PV=PMT\frac{1-(1+i)^{-n}}{i}$$

$$PV=300\frac{1-(1+0.0060)^{-24}}{0.0060}$$

$$PV\approx 6686.98$$

The annuity present value is $\$6{,}686.98$, so the statement is True.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 2
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: At a continuously compounded annual rate of $4.5\%$, the doubling time is $15.90$ years to the nearest $0.01$ year.
A debt of $\$18{,}000$ is due in $30$ months. At a nominal annual rate of $6.0\%$ compounded monthly, its present value is $\$15{,}498.54$ to the nearest cent.
A maintenance plan pays $\$1{,}600$ now, then each later annual payment is $72\%$ of the preceding payment forever. The undiscounted sum of all payments is $\$5{,}789.29$ to the nearest cent.
At an effective annual rate of $4.5\%$, an annuity-due of $8$ level annual payments has a present value exactly $4.5\%$ larger than the corresponding ordinary annuity.
A mortgage of $\$180{,}000$ is repaid by $300$ equal month-end payments at a monthly rate of $0.450\%$. The required payment is $\$1{,}109.63$ to the nearest cent.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

Continuous doubling time is found by solving the exponential growth equation for time.

$$2=e^{rt}$$

$$\ln 2=rt$$

$$t=\frac{\ln 2}{0.045}\approx 15.40$$

The doubling time is $15.40$ years, not $15.90$ years, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

Monthly discounting matches the nominal rate conversion to the number of months.

$$i_m=\frac{0.060}{12}=0.005000$$

$$PV=\frac{18000}{(1+0.005000)^{30}}$$

$$PV\approx 15498.54$$

The monthly-discounted value is $\$15{,}498.54$, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

An infinite geometric series converges when the common ratio has absolute value below one.

$$S_\infty=\frac{a}{1-r}$$

$$S_\infty=\frac{1600}{1-0.72}$$

$$S_\infty\approx 5714.29$$

The convergent total is $\$5{,}714.29$, not $\$5{,}789.29$, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

Moving every annuity payment one period earlier multiplies present value by one plus the periodic rate.

$$PV_{\mathrm{due}}=(1+i)PV_{\mathrm{ordinary}}$$

$$PV_{\mathrm{ordinary}}=1000\frac{1-(1+0.045)^{-8}}{0.045}\approx 6595.89$$

$$PV_{\mathrm{due}}=(1+0.045)(6595.89)\approx 6892.70$$

$$\frac{PV_{\mathrm{due}}-PV_{\mathrm{ordinary}}}{PV_{\mathrm{ordinary}}}=0.045$$

The annuity-due premium is exactly $4.5\%$, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

A level-payment mortgage sets the loan principal equal to an ordinary-annuity present value.

$$PMT=P\frac{i}{1-(1+i)^{-n}}$$

$$PMT=180000\frac{0.004500}{1-(1+0.004500)^{-300}}$$

$$PMT\approx 1094.63$$

The required payment is $\$1{,}094.63$, not $\$1{,}109.63$, so the statement is False.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 3
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A cash-flow stream pays $\$3{,}000$ in one year, $\$4{,}500$ in two years, and $\$5{,}500$ in three years. At $7.0\%$ effective annual interest, its present value is $\$11{,}223.85$ to the nearest cent.

A saver deposits $\$500$ at the end of year $1$ and increases each later annual deposit by $8\%$. The account earns $5.0\%$ effective annually. Immediately after the year $5$ deposit, the balance is $\$3{,}272.44$ to the nearest cent.
A perpetuity pays $\$750$ at each year-end, with the first payment one year from now. At $4.0\%$ effective annual interest, its present value is $\$18{,}750.00$.
A $\$180{,}000$ mortgage has $300$ monthly payments at $0.450\%$ per month. Immediately after payment $48$, the outstanding balance is $\$165{,}787.83$ to the nearest cent.

A project costs $\$9{,}000$ now and pays $\$3{,}800$, $\$4{,}200$, and $\$4{,}600$ at the ends of years $1$, $2$, and $3$. At a discount rate of $8.0\%$, its NPV is $\$1{,}770.97$ to the nearest cent.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

A cash-flow stream is valued by discounting each dated payment separately and then adding.

$$PV_1=\frac{3000}{1+0.070}\approx 2803.74$$

$$PV_2=\frac{4500}{(1+0.070)^2}\approx 3930.47$$

$$PV_3=\frac{5500}{(1+0.070)^3}\approx 4489.64$$

$$PV=PV_1+PV_2+PV_3\approx 11223.85$$

The stream is worth $\$11{,}223.85$ today, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

At the valuation date, growing deposits form a geometric series after each receives its remaining interest.

$$FV=500(1.050)^{4}\sum_{k=0}^{4}\left(\frac{1.08}{1.050}\right)^k$$

$$FV=500(1.050)^{4}\frac{1-(1.028571)^{5}}{1-1.028571}$$

$$FV\approx 3217.44$$

The accumulated balance is $\$3{,}217.44$, not $\$3{,}272.44$, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

A level perpetuity with its first payment one period ahead has value equal to payment divided by rate.

$$PV=\frac{C}{i}$$

$$PV=\frac{750}{0.040}$$

$$PV=18750.00$$

The perpetuity value is $\$18{,}750.00$, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

Immediately after a payment, the mortgage balance is the present value of all remaining payments.

$$PMT=180000\frac{0.004500}{1-(1+0.004500)^{-300}}\approx 1094.63$$

$$n_{\mathrm{remaining}}=300-48=252$$

$$B_{48}=1094.63\frac{1-(1+0.004500)^{-252}}{0.004500}$$

$$B_{48}\approx 164787.83$$

The outstanding balance is $\$164{,}787.83$, not $\$165{,}787.83$, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

Net present value adds discounted inflows to the signed initial cash flow.

$$NPV=-9000+\frac{3800}{1+0.080}+\frac{4200}{(1+0.080)^2}+\frac{4600}{(1+0.080)^3}$$

$$NPV\approx-9000+3518.52+3600.82+3651.63$$

$$NPV\approx 1770.97$$

The project NPV is $\$1{,}770.97$, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Topics: 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6, 3.7. A checks present value of dated cash flows; B checks geometrically growing deposits; C checks level perpetuity valuation; D checks outstanding mortgage balance; E checks multi-period NPV.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 4
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A lease charges $\$1{,}200$ in year $1$ and raises the charge by $6.0\%$ each year. Over $7$ years, the total charge is $\$10{,}167.61$ to the nearest cent.
A growing perpetuity pays $\$900$ one year from now, and later payments grow by $2.5\%$ annually. At a discount rate of $7.5\%$, its present value is $\$18{,}000.00$.
A $\$180{,}000$ mortgage uses $300$ level monthly payments at $0.450\%$ per month. In the first payment, $\$304.63$ reduces principal.
A project costs $\$5{,}000$ now and has one inflow of $\$6{,}050.00$ at the end of year $2$. Its effective annual IRR is $10.00\%$.
At the same nominal annual rate of $8.4\%$, monthly compounding produces a lower effective annual rate than quarterly compounding.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

Repeated proportional escalation makes the lease charges consecutive terms of one geometric progression.

$$a_{7}=1200(1.06)^{6}\approx 1702.22$$

$$S_{7}=1200\frac{1.06^{7}-1}{1.06-1}$$

$$S_{7}\approx 10072.61$$

The lease total is $\$10{,}072.61$, not $\$10{,}167.61$, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

A growing perpetuity uses the first next-period payment divided by the discount-growth spread.

$$PV=\frac{C_1}{i-g}$$

$$PV=\frac{900}{0.075-0.025}$$

$$PV=18000.00$$

The growing-perpetuity value is $\$18{,}000.00$, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

Each mortgage payment first covers current interest, with the remainder reducing principal.

$$PMT=180000\frac{0.004500}{1-(1+0.004500)^{-300}}\approx 1094.63$$

$$I_1=180000(0.004500)=810.00$$

$$PR_1=1094.63-810.00=284.63$$

The first principal reduction is $\$284.63$, not $\$304.63$, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

For one initial outflow and one terminal inflow, the IRR equates the terminal value to compounded cost.

$$5000(1+r)^{2}=6050.00$$

$$1+r=\left(\frac{6050.00}{5000}\right)^{1/2}$$

$$100r=10.00\%$$

The effective annual IRR is $10.00\%$, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

For a fixed positive nominal rate, more frequent compounding produces a larger effective rate.

$$R_{12}=\left(1+\frac{0.084}{12}\right)^{12}-1\approx 0.087311$$

$$R_4=\left(1+\frac{0.084}{4}\right)^4-1\approx 0.086683$$

$$0.087311>0.086683$$

Monthly compounding is not the lower-rate option, so the statement is False.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 5
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: An ordinary annuity pays $\$325$ at each month-end for $30$ months. At a monthly rate of $0.65\%$, its present value is $\$8{,}832.30$ to the nearest cent.
A $\$180{,}000$ mortgage is amortized over $300$ months at $0.450\%$ per month with level payments. Total interest over the full schedule is $\$150{,}890.16$ to the nearest cent.
A project costs $\$10{,}000$ and pays $\$4{,}200$, $\$4{,}300$, and $\$4{,}400$ after one, two, and three years. Under the NPV rule at $9.0\%$, the project should be accepted.
An effective annual rate of $7.5\%$ is equivalent to a monthly rate of $0.624\%$ to the nearest $0.001$ percentage point.
A force of interest of $4.0\%$ per year corresponds to an effective annual rate of $4.08\%$ to the nearest $0.01$ percentage point.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

An ordinary-annuity present value discounts a level payment made at each period-end.

$$PV=PMT\frac{1-(1+i)^{-n}}{i}$$

$$PV=325\frac{1-(1+0.0065)^{-30}}{0.0065}$$

$$PV\approx 8832.30$$

The annuity present value is $\$8{,}832.30$, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

Total mortgage interest equals all scheduled payments minus the original principal.

$$PMT=180000\frac{0.004500}{1-(1+0.004500)^{-300}}\approx 1094.63$$

$$\sum PMT=300(1094.63385133)\approx 328390.16$$

$$I=328390.16-180000=148390.16$$

The full-schedule interest is $\$148{,}390.16$, not $\$150{,}890.16$, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

The NPV decision rule accepts a standalone project exactly when discounted value is positive.

$$NPV=-10000+\frac{4200}{1+0.090}+\frac{4300}{(1+0.090)^2}+\frac{4400}{(1+0.090)^3}$$

$$NPV\approx 870.04$$

$$NPV >0$$

The NPV rule gives acceptance, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

Equivalent rates have the same annual accumulation factor.

$$(1+i_m)^{12}=1+0.075$$

$$i_m=(1+0.075)^{1/12}-1$$

$$100i_m\approx 0.604\%$$

The equivalent monthly rate is $0.604\%$, not $0.624\%$, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

A one-year continuously compounded rate converts through the exponential growth factor.

$$1+R=e^{0.040}$$

$$R=e^{0.040}-1\approx 0.040811$$

$$100R\approx 4.08\%$$

The effective annual rate is $4.08\%$, so the statement is True.

tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A mortgage of $\$190{,}000$ is repaid by $312$ equal month-end payments at a monthly rate of $0.475\%$. The required payment is $\$1{,}184.01$ to the nearest cent.
A project costs $\$8{,}000$ now, pays $\$3{,}000$ in one year, and $\$6{,}675.20$ in two years. An effective annual rate of $12.0\%$ is its IRR.
An investment of $\$6{,}000$ at a nominal $6.0\%$ compounded quarterly for $3$ years grows to $\$7{,}248.71$ to the nearest cent.
A payment of $\$14{,}000$ due in $5$ years is discounted continuously at $3.8\%$. Its present value is $\$11{,}577.43$ to the nearest cent.
A contract pays $\$2{,}500$ at the ends of years $1$, $3$, and $5$. At $5.5\%$ effective annual interest, the contract is worth $\$6{,}496.54$ today to the nearest cent.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

A level-payment mortgage sets the loan principal equal to an ordinary-annuity present value.

$$PMT=P\frac{i}{1-(1+i)^{-n}}$$

$$PMT=190000\frac{0.004750}{1-(1+0.004750)^{-312}}$$

$$PMT\approx 1169.01$$

The required payment is $\$1{,}169.01$, not $\$1{,}184.01$, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

A candidate IRR is correct only when discounting every project cash flow at that rate gives zero NPV.

$$NPV(0.120)=-8000+\frac{3000}{1+0.120}+\frac{6675.20}{(1+0.120)^2}$$

$$NPV(0.120)\approx 0.00$$

The candidate rate makes NPV zero, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

Periodic compounding uses the quarterly rate and the total number of quarters.

$$i=\frac{0.060}{4},\quad n=4(3)=12$$

$$FV=6000\left(1+\frac{0.060}{4}\right)^{12}$$

$$FV\approx 7173.71$$

The accumulated value is $\$7{,}173.71$, not $\$7{,}248.71$, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

Continuous present value reverses exponential accumulation with a negative exponent.

$$PV=Fe^{-rt}$$

$$PV=14000e^{-0.038(5)}$$

$$PV\approx 11577.43$$

The present value is $\$11{,}577.43$, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

Irregularly timed payments must each use the discount exponent matching their own date.

$$PV=\frac{2500}{1+0.055}+\frac{2500}{(1+0.055)^3}+\frac{2500}{(1+0.055)^5}$$

$$PV\approx 2369.67+2129.03+1912.84$$

$$PV\approx 6411.54$$

The contract value is $\$6{,}411.54$, not $\$6{,}496.54$, so the statement is False.

$$NPV(0.140)=-9200+\frac{3400}{1+0.140}+\frac{8080.32}{(1+0.140)^2}$$

$$NPV(0.140)\approx 0.00$$

The candidate rate makes NPV zero, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

Periodic compounding uses the quarterly rate and the total number of quarters.

$$i=\frac{0.070}{4},\quad n=4(5)=20$$

$$FV=8000\left(1+\frac{0.070}{4}\right)^{20}$$

$$FV\approx 11318.23$$

The accumulated value is $\$11{,}318.23$, not $\$11{,}393.23$, so the statement is False.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 19
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A perpetuity pays $\$900$ at each year-end, with the first payment one year from now. At $5.5\%$ effective annual interest, its present value is $\$16{,}363.64$.
A $\$210{,}000$ mortgage has $336$ monthly payments at $0.525\%$ per month. Immediately after payment $84$, the outstanding balance is $\$186{,}874.06$ to the nearest cent.

A project costs $\$11{,}250$ now and pays $\$4{,}400$, $\$4{,}950$, and $\$5{,}500$ at the ends of years $1$, $2$, and $3$. At a discount rate of $9.5\%$, its NPV is $\$1{,}085.72$ to the nearest cent.
A nominal annual rate of $9.0\%$ compounded $365$ times per year has an effective annual rate of $9.52\%$ to the nearest $0.01$ percentage point.
An account starts at $\$9{,}250$ and grows continuously at $5.0\%$ for $7$ years. Its balance is $\$13{,}126.37$ to the nearest cent.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

A level perpetuity with its first payment one period ahead has value equal to payment divided by rate.

$$PV=\frac{C}{i}$$

$$PV=\frac{900}{0.055}$$

$$PV=16363.64$$

The perpetuity value is $\$16{,}363.64$, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

Immediately after a payment, the mortgage balance is the present value of all remaining payments.

$$PMT=210000\frac{0.005250}{1-(1+0.005250)^{-336}}\approx 1331.76$$

$$n_{\mathrm{remaining}}=336-84=252$$

$$B_{84}=1331.76\frac{1-(1+0.005250)^{-252}}{0.005250}$$

$$B_{84}\approx 185874.06$$

The outstanding balance is $\$185{,}874.06$, not $\$186{,}874.06$, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

Net present value adds discounted inflows to the signed initial cash flow.

$$NPV=-11250+\frac{4400}{1+0.095}+\frac{4950}{(1+0.095)^2}+\frac{5500}{(1+0.095)^3}$$

$$NPV\approx-11250+4018.26+4128.35+4189.10$$

$$NPV\approx 1085.72$$

The project NPV is $\$1{,}085.72$, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

The effective annual rate compounds the periodic nominal rate over every period in the year.

$$R=\left(1+\frac{0.090}{365}\right)^{365}-1$$

$$R\approx 0.094200$$

$$100R\approx 9.42\%$$

The rounded effective rate is $9.42\%$, not $9.52\%$, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

Continuous compounding applies the exponential accumulation factor.

$$FV=Pe^{rt}$$

$$FV=9250e^{0.050(7)}$$

$$FV\approx 13126.37$$

The continuous balance is $\$13{,}126.37$, so the statement is True.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 20
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A $\$210{,}000$ mortgage uses $336$ level monthly payments at $0.525\%$ per month. In the first payment, $\$249.26$ reduces principal.
A project costs $\$6{,}500$ now and has one inflow of $\$11{,}975.83$ at the end of year $5$. Its effective annual IRR is $13.00\%$.
At the same nominal annual rate of $9.6\%$, monthly compounding produces a lower effective annual rate than quarterly compounding.
At a continuously compounded annual rate of $6.0\%$, the doubling time is $11.55$ years to the nearest $0.01$ year.
A debt of $\$21{,}000$ is due in $48$ months. At a nominal annual rate of $7.2\%$ compounded monthly, its present value is $\$15{,}848.55$ to the nearest cent.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

Each mortgage payment first covers current interest, with the remainder reducing principal.

$$PMT=210000\frac{0.005250}{1-(1+0.005250)^{-336}}\approx 1331.76$$

$$I_1=210000(0.005250)=1102.50$$

$$PR_1=1331.76-1102.50=229.26$$

The first principal reduction is $\$229.26$, not $\$249.26$, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

For one initial outflow and one terminal inflow, the IRR equates the terminal value to compounded cost.

$$6500(1+r)^{5}=11975.83$$

$$1+r=\left(\frac{11975.83}{6500}\right)^{1/5}$$

$$100r=13.00\%$$

The effective annual IRR is $13.00\%$, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

For a fixed positive nominal rate, more frequent compounding produces a larger effective rate.

$$R_{12}=\left(1+\frac{0.096}{12}\right)^{12}-1\approx 0.100339$$

$$R_4=\left(1+\frac{0.096}{4}\right)^4-1\approx 0.099512$$

$$0.100339>0.099512$$

Monthly compounding is not the lower-rate option, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

Continuous doubling time is found by solving the exponential growth equation for time.

$$2=e^{rt}$$

$$\ln 2=rt$$

$$t=\frac{\ln 2}{0.060}\approx 11.55$$

The doubling time is $11.55$ years, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

Monthly discounting matches the nominal rate conversion to the number of months.

$$i_m=\frac{0.072}{12}=0.006000$$

$$PV=\frac{21000}{(1+0.006000)^{48}}$$

$$PV\approx 15758.55$$

The monthly-discounted value is $\$15{,}758.55$, not $\$15{,}848.55$, so the statement is False.
